about.heading: about
about.headline: crafting next-generation tools for playful learning

pillars.description: I build research-backed, active learning experiences where learners have to get hands-on and turn their minds on.
I build content-specific tools that make concepts interactive in ways one-size-fits-all content delivery can't.
I build tools that teach more than information, targeting concepts, higher-order skills, and learner dispositions.

blocks.text: 11 years designing playful, hands-on learning as a classroom teacher taught me what rich learning looks like and today's EdTech has a long way to go. My graduate study and ongoing teaching at Harvard have kept me plugged in to the latest research on digital learning and play.
highlight: graduate study and ongoing teaching at Harvard

blocks.text: In my 5 years designing and product mananging learning games at ST Math, I led the development of 27 innovative games and 9 accessibility features across 3 products, reaching more than 2 million K-12 students and 174,000+ educators in 7,400+ schools.
highlight: designing and product mananging learning games at ST Math

pieces.title: TREASURE BOX
pieces.subtitle: A suite of innovative place value learning games I designed for ST Math
overview: Treasure Box is a suite of 6 learning games I designed for ST Math. Going beyond math tools that merely quiz students on place value, carrying, and borrowing as abstract concepts, Treasure Box lets students concretely compose, decompose, and regroup numbers with unique digital manipulatives designed from the ground up to teach these concepts. Spanning 3rd–6th grade Common Core and Texas standards, it remains the largest game development effort in ST Math's history, and is currently played by more than a million students every school year.
pieces.disclosures: Treasure Box art by Pamela Tseng. Video music: "drunken sailors" by ALKAKRAB, used with permission. Treasure Box was developed by MIND Education. This footage is shared for portfolio purposes to showcase my work as Lead Designer on the project. All rights to Treasure Box belong to MIND Education.

pieces.title: MEMORY METRO
pieces.subtitle: A memory + math game prototype developed solo with Claude Code
overview: This unpublished prototype, solo designed and developed with Claude Code for a project at MIND Education, has two learning goals: build math fact fluency and strengthen working memory. Avoiding visual and thematic complexity, the design uses a small number of elegant, intuitive mechanics to generate a wide range of levels full of discovery, surprise, and humor, while precisely titrating both mathematical and working-memory difficulty as students progress. The result is a compact but expressive design system that reflects my focused approach to learning game design.
pieces.disclosures: Memory Metro is an unpublished prototype I designed and developed solo during my time at MIND Education. It is shared here for portfolio purposes only and is not an official or released MIND Education product.

pieces.title: VARIABLE PIPES
pieces.subtitle: A game that explores variable substitution, and true and false solution sets designed for ST Math
overview: I designed this learning game about variables, expressions, equations, and inequalities for ST Math, a game-based, K-8, supplemental math product. The game targets 6th grade Common Core (CC) standards and allows learners to playfully interact with multi-variable expressions, equations, and inequalities. Through these interactions, learners build a conceptual understanding of variable substitution, true and false equations and inequalities, and solution sets.
pieces.disclosures: Variable Pipes art by Joel Conklin. Variable Pipes was developed by MIND Education. This footage is shared for portfolio purposes to showcase my work as Lead Designer on the project. All rights to Variable Pipes belong to MIND Education.

pieces.title: THE GREENFIELD GAME
pieces.subtitle: A classroom-based simulation where students run a small town and make decisions about economics, government, and infrastructure
pieces.details: Teacher & Curriculum Designer | Greenfield Center School | 2015
overview: The Greenfield Game is a classroom learning game iteratively developed over five years of my time as a 2nd/3rd grade classroom teacher at Greenfield Center School. The project is designed to answer the grade-appropriate questions: "What is a town?" and "How do towns work?" First students visit key places in town and then co-create a simulation of how the people, places, and jobs that they visited interconnect. In the course of the game students make individual and collective decisions about economics, government, infrastructure, and social issues.
pieces.disclosures: Music used in this video: "Cape Cod Kwassa Kwassa" by Vampire Weekend, "Bizness" by Tune-Yards, and "No Intention" by Dirty Projectors. This video was created for an in-school museum installation and is shared here for portfolio purposes only. No copyright infringement is intended, and I do not hold a license for this music.

pieces.title: MIGRATION DATA POETRY PROJECT
pieces.subtitle: A whole-school project combining migration data and poetry to explore the complex reality of international migration
pieces.details: Teacher & Curriculum Designer | Greenfield Center School | 2019
overview: The Migration Data Poetry Project is an interdisciplinary, whole-school project I designed as a classroom teacher at the Greenfield Center School. The project attempts to answer questions about who today's migrants are, where they come from, migrate to, and why, without reducing their stories to economic trends and simplistic tropes. Using data from the U.N. International Migration Report, I generated poem prompts that invited students from across the school to imagine the unique stories of individual migrants. The result was more than 100 poems exploring the diverse, multi-faceted reality of international migration.

pieces.title: THE DRESS REHEARSAL DID NOT GO WELL
pieces.subtitle: A puzzle game built in 48 hours for a game jam with the theme 'Roles Reversed'
overview: A puzzle game about mice and frogs putting on a play that refuses to go smoothly. Created in 48 hours for the 2023 GMTK Game Jam around the theme "Roles Reversed," the game casts players as a stage-side puzzle solver: swap the masks worn by the actors to change how they move, and guide the show's two sweethearts to meet on the same square before the curtain call. I served as Lead Designer and Programmer, with art by Nathaniel Klein.

pieces_hidden.title: CREATIVE DECIMAL DIVISION
pieces_hidden.subtitle: A playful, visual decimal division game designed for ST Math
overview: I designed this fine-art-themed decimal division learning game for ST Math, a game-based, K-8, supplemental math product. This game targets 5th and 6th grade Common Core standards using an original, visual model of the partial product division strategy. Players explore decimal division in flexible, hands-on game modes, before solidifying their understanding in number and algorithm-based modes.
pieces_hidden.disclosures: Creative Decimal Division art by Pamela Tseng. Creative Decimal Division was developed by MIND Education. This footage is shared for portfolio purposes to showcase my work as Lead Designer on the project. All rights to Creative Decimal Division belong to MIND Education.
